svg.title: Wireframe chapter 3 (desktop 1280px): Pedestrians are 1 in 14 of the injured, but 1 in 4 of those who die in hospital

g.text: injured, but 1 in 4 of those who
Counting admissions treats a sprained wrist and a fractured skull
the same. Look at what happens after admission and a different road
user comes to the top of the list.
Pedestrians were 7.3% of road-crash admissions, but 26.4% of the people who died in
Of every 1,000 pedestrians admitted, about 22 died in hospital. For car drivers it
was about 6, and for cyclists about 2.
For pedestrians aged 75 and over it was 61 in 1,000, and survivors stayed an average
Pedestrians take up twice their share of hospital beds
Notes: Share of admissions and bed days, 2016-2021; deaths in hospital, 2011-2019. Shares are of all road users, so the five bars do not sum to 100%. These are
For pedestrians over 75, one admission in 16 ends in death
open dot: all road users | dark dot + whisker: pedestrians
Notes: Per 1,000 people admitted, not per head of population. Deaths within hospital stays, 2011-2019; average stay (days per person who left hospital alive),
Apart from rare train collisions, a heavy vehicle or bus is the
deadliest thing to be hit by
open: all road users | dark: pedestrians
Notes: Rates shown only where there are at least 100 cases and 10 deaths, 2011-2019. Train collisions are higher still but rest on very few deaths: 17 in nine
These figures describe what happens to people once they reach hospital. Most road deaths
happen at the scene and never appear in this data.
